reading: Every foreground run shifts one cell left (cells pushed past the left edge are lost); then the background 0 becomes 5.
why: output = input shifted by (0,-1) with clipping at the left border, then 0->5, other colours unchanged
invariants: run lengths except where clipped at the left edge

reading: Full separator rows of colour c become 1 (with 8 where they cross the vertical 8 line). Every other row is painted the colour of its nearest separator row, with the 8 line cell becoming 1. A row exactly halfway between two separators of different colours becomes all 1.

slots.separators: full rows with no background-7 cells; their colour c is the non-1 colour
slots.band row: non-separator row; 7->c of nearest separator row, 8->1
slots.tie row: equidistant from separators of different colours -> whole row 1 (same colour on both sides -> that colour)

why: each row's colour is decided by distance to separator rows only; the vertical line column stays a line (1 in bands, 8 on separators)

reading: There are two shape kinds, each in its own colour and repeated. Every copy of shape A is replaced by shape B in B's colour, and every copy of B by A in A's colour, aligned at the bounding box top-left.

slots.shape A: the single shape (8-connected) of the first colour, all copies identical
slots.shape B: the single shape of the second colour
slots.anchor: top-left of each copy's bounding box

why: exactly two colours, each colour's components are translates of one shape; output has each component replaced by the other colour's shape

reading: Each single coloured cell on the 8 background moves by an offset fixed by its colour: 7 up 2, 9 down 2, 2 left 2, 1 right 1.
why: each marker's displacement depends only on its colour and is identical across pairs

reading: Each 1 sitting on top of a 5 pillar drops to the bottom row in its column, replacing the 5 there; its old cell becomes background.

slots.subject: the colour-1 cells
slots.target: bottom border row of the same column

why: every 1 ends in the bottom row of its own column; the 5 pillar cells above the bottom row are unchanged

reading: Colour-2 cells form clusters (2-cells within 2 steps of each other); every non-2 cell inside a cluster's bounding box becomes 4.

new_rows.name: two_box
new_rows.datalog:
two(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, 2).
near(Y1, X1, Y2, X2) :- two(Y1, X1), two(Y2, X2), DY = Y2 - Y1, DX = X2 - X1, DY >= -2, DY <= 2, DX >= -2, DX <= 2.
same(Y1, X1, Y2, X2) :- near(Y1, X1, Y2, X2).
same(Y1, X1, Y3, X3) :- same(Y1, X1, Y2, X2), near(Y2, X2, Y3, X3).
loy(Y1, X1, min(Y2)) :- same(Y1, X1, Y2, X2).
hiy(Y1, X1, max(Y2)) :- same(Y1, X1, Y2, X2).
lox(Y1, X1, min(X2)) :- same(Y1, X1, Y2, X2).
hix(Y1, X1, max(X2)) :- same(Y1, X1, Y2, X2).
two_box(Y, X) :- two(Y1, X1), loy(Y1, X1, A), hiy(Y1, X1, B), lox(Y1, X1, L), hix(Y1, X1, R), px(Y, X, C), Y >= A, Y <= B, X >= L, X <= R, !two(Y, X).

why: every changed cell lies in the bounding box of a 2-cluster (Chebyshev distance <= 2 linking) and becomes 4; nothing outside those boxes changes
invariants: every cell outside the cluster boxes

reading: Draw a vertical bar of 5 up from the bottom row, two columns right of the rightmost bar; its height is (number of 8 cells) minus (number of 2 cells).
why: on every pair the only change is a 5 bar of that height at that column, anchored at the bottom

reading: The shape has an outer colour (the topmost cell's colour) and an inner colour. Every background cell that touches an outer cell diagonally but touches no outer cell orthogonally becomes the inner colour, growing the diagonal lattice by one layer.

new_rows.name: diag_ring
new_rows.datalog:
top(min(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
outer(C) :- top(Y), cell(Y, X, C).
oc(Y, X) :- outer(C), cell(Y, X, C).
fgc(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
ortho(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), DY = 0.
ortho(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), DX = 0.
diag(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), !ortho(DY, DX).
nd(Y2, X2) :- oc(Y, X), diag(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX.
no(Y2, X2) :- oc(Y, X), ortho(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX.
diag_ring(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), nd(Y, X), !fgc(Y, X), !no(Y, X).

slots.colour: the inner colour (the foreground colour other than the topmost cell's colour); varies per pair

why: the added cells are exactly the diag_ring cells and all take the inner colour

reading: A box of outer colour holds an inner core of a second colour. A band of the core colour is drawn around the box. Its uniform thickness is the core's smaller side, capped by the space to the nearest grid edge.

slots.subject: the single two-colour box (outer ring + inner core)
slots.thickness: min(core height, core width, distance from box to nearest grid edge)

why: the only new cells are background cells within Chebyshev distance k of the box, all in the core colour

reading: Each 8 L-tromino (a 2x2 block missing one cell) gets its missing cell filled with 1.

new_rows.name: l_hole
new_rows.datalog:
fgc(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
inblk(Y, X, Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C).
inblk(Y, X, Y2, X2) :- px(Y, X, C), off(DY, DX), DY >= 0, DX >= 0, Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, px(Y2, X2, C2).
bfg(Y, X, count(Y2, X2)) :- inblk(Y, X, Y2, X2), fgc(Y2, X2).
l_hole(Y2, X2) :- bfg(Y, X, N), N = 3, inblk(Y, X, Y2, X2), !fgc(Y2, X2).

why: every changed cell is the single background cell of a 2x2 block holding three 8s, and becomes 1
